pk.context: 7.5 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

pill.desc: pastel yellow, uncoated, round biconvex tablet

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is 89%, and a high-fat meal raises peak levels about 22% without changing total exposure. It is 99.4% protein bound and cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 351.4, and it is practically insoluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in two strengths, 7.5 mg and 15 mg, and reaches steady state by day 5 of dosing.
clues.safety: Boxed warning on serious cardiovascular and gastrointestinal events. Contraindicated around bypass graft surgery and after aspirin allergy; abdominal pain and vomiting are common.
clues.indication: Relief of the signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, and of juvenile rheumatoid arthritis in patients weighing at least 60 kg.
clues.mechanism: It involves inhibition of cyclooxygenase, COX-1 and COX-2, which reduces prostaglandin synthesis; the precise action is not completely understood.

tell: A second concentration peak at 12 to 14 hours, from biliary recycling, sets this NSAID apart.
